original_question: Let d be an integer that is not divisible√by n-th powers of primes, let xn − d be an irreducible polynomial over Q, let θ = n d, and let K = Q(θ) be the radical extension of degree n of the field Q. The multiplicative group K ∗ of the field K is canonically embedded into the group AutQ(K) of all invertible Q-linear mappings of the Q-space K; let T be the image of K ∗ under this embedding. In the natural basis 1, θ, θ2,..., θn−1 of the Q-space K the group AutQ(K) corresponds to G = GL(n, Q), and the subgroup T to a subgroup T(d) (unsplit maximal torus). Every subgroup H of G containing T(d) and some one-dimensional transformation is rich in elementary transvections(V. A. Koibaev, St. Petersbg. Math. J., 21, no. 5(2010), 731–742) and thus defines a net σ = σ(H) (V. A. Koibaev, A. V. Shilov, J. Math. Sci. New York 171, no. 3(2010), 380–385). Let E(σ) denote the subgroup generated by all transvections in the net group G(σ). Is it true that H ⩽ NG(E(σ))? This inclusion was proved in the case n = 2(V. A. Koibaev, Dokl. Math., 41, no. 3(1990), 414–416).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.77 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of the current arXiv version of The Kourovka Notebook. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it includes the radical extension K = Q(θ), the canonical embedding of K* into Aut_Q(K), the identification with G = GL(n, Q) in the basis 1, θ, θ^2, ..., θ^(n−1), the unsplit maximal torus T(d), the hypothesis that H contains T(d) and a one-dimensional transformation, the associated net σ(H), the subgroup E(σ) generated by transvections in G(σ), and the final inclusion question H ≤ N_G(E(σ)); it also records that the inclusion is known for n = 2. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The draft has minor OCR/typesetting damage that should be repaired to match the paper exactly, especially in the phrases "not divisible by n-th powers of primes" and "θ = √[n]{d}". ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

To be fully stand-alone, it should say explicitly that Aut_Q(K) is being used here for the group of all invertible Q-linear maps of the Q-vector space K, not merely field automorphisms. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

It should make explicit that the question is about every subgroup H ≤ G = GL(n, Q) containing T(d) and some one-dimensional transformation. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

It should spell out that σ means the net σ(H) attached to H, and that E(σ) is generated by all transvections in the associated net group G(σ). ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
It should define N_G(E(σ)) explicitly as the normalizer of E(σ) in G. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

If the question is meant to be readable without consulting the cited net-theoretic papers, the terms "one-dimensional transformation," "net," "net group," and "transvection" remain specialized and are not locally redefined in Problem 21.77 itself. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Fix an integer n ≥ 2, let d be an integer not divisible by n-th powers of primes, assume x^n − d is irreducible over Q, set θ = √[n]{d}, and let K = Q(θ). Embed K* into Aut_Q(K) by multiplication maps x ↦ ax, where Aut_Q(K) denotes the group of all invertible Q-linear maps of the Q-vector space K, and let T be the image. Via the basis 1, θ, θ^2, ..., θ^(n−1), identify Aut_Q(K) with G = GL(n, Q), and let T(d) be the corresponding unsplit maximal torus. If H ≤ G contains T(d) and a one-dimensional transformation, let σ = σ(H) be the associated net, let G(σ) be the corresponding net group, and let E(σ) be the subgroup of G(σ) generated by all transvections. Must H lie in the normalizer N_G(E(σ)) of E(σ) in G? ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim transcription of Problem 21.77 in the current arXiv version of the paper, so the sharpest paper-faithful refinement is to preserve that exact setup and only normalize notation, repair OCR glitches, and make the embedding and normalizer notation explicit. I did not broaden the problem or invent a new variant, and I did not supply an alternate formulation because no explicit equivalent reformulation is given nearby in the paper itself. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300))
